products.name: iPhone 17
products.value_context: The iPhone 17 offers luxury features at a high price, appealing to brand loyalists.
pros: 120Hz refresh rate on a 6.3-inch OLED display.
48 MP dual rear cameras for high-quality photos.
Strong ecosystem integration with Apple services.
cons: Limited RAM at 8 GB compared to competitors.
products.best_for: Ideal for Apple enthusiasts seeking a premium experience with a strong ecosystem.

products.name: Galaxy S25 Ultra
products.value_context: The Galaxy S25 Ultra provides superior specs and performance for its price in the GCC market.
pros: 200 MP main camera for professional-grade photography.
Snapdragon 8 Elite processor for top performance.
cons: Some users report quick battery drain under heavy use.
products.best_for: Best for users needing top-tier performance and camera capabilities at a competitive price.

review_summary.consensus: The Apple iPhone 17 is widely regarded as a strong entry-level model, offering excellent performance and a high-quality camera system. Reviewers appreciate its display and overall usability, though some note the high price point.

highlights.point: [4] The iPhone 17 is the best basic iPhone ever, featuring a smoother, bigger display, excellent overall performance and some genuinely useful features.
[9] The iPhone 17 starts at $829, meaning there hasn't been a price increase over last year's model.
[2] With pricing starting at $1,399 AUD, nobody sane could call the iPhone 17 'cheap'.
[10] The display features a 6.3-inch Super Retina XDR display with a 120Hz refresh rate.

review_summary.consensus: The Samsung Galaxy S25 Ultra showcases impressive specifications, particularly in its camera capabilities and processing power. However, some users have expressed concerns regarding battery performance and the incremental nature of its upgrades compared to previous models.

highlights.point: [1] Quad-camera system with ultra-high-resolution and advanced zoom capabilities for professional-grade photography.
[2] Features a Snapdragon 8 Elite Fast Processor, enhancing overall performance.
[3] The 5000mAh battery provides substantial power, but some users report it drains quickly under heavy use.
[7] Camera specs include a 200 MP main sensor, which is a significant upgrade for photography enthusiasts.
[9] The pricing remains competitive compared to its predecessor, which may appeal to potential buyers.
[10] Some reviews indicate that the improvements feel incremental rather than groundbreaking.
